text:
morgan: heads-up — infra-builder promotion to prod failed on manifest verification during the image-publish job. CI shows SBOM signature mismatch and the manifest list order looks different than the one we published earlier.

deploy-bot: build#4123 failed: exit code 1. log excerpt:
```
> verifying cosign signature for image registry.redwood/tools/infra-builder:stable
> signature mismatch: signed manifest digest sha256:aaa... != resolved digest sha256:bbb...
```

ian: looking. last successful publish was yesterday at 03:12 UTC. we rotated the cosign key this morning — could be related. also noticed the manifest list was rebuilt by the registry and reordered arches (arm64/amd64) which changes the manifest list digest.

sasha: yeah many registries canonicalize manifest lists differently. we shouldn't trust manifest-list digests for signature checks unless we pin by image manifest digest (the single-arch digest) or sign the image by digest after the registry finalizes it.

lisa: reminder — the builder image builds pull in a base image that we pin by tag in Dockerfile (ubuntu:22.04) but not by digest. a base rebuild could change layering and the SBOM. that's probably why cosign sees a different payload.

morgan: options: 1) pin base to digest in builder Dockerfile and force rebuild; 2) sign the final digest after push using a short job that resolves the digest and cosign-signs that digest; 3) relax verification to accept equivalent manifests (not great). which is least effort?

ian: least risky: sign final digest after push. pipeline change: publish -> resolve digest with `crane digest` or `skopeo inspect` -> cosign sign $digest. cheap step.

sasha: example command to resolve and sign (add to publish job):
```
DIGEST=$(crane digest registry.redwood/tools/infra-builder:stable)
cosign sign --key $COSIGN_KEY registry.redwood/tools/infra-builder@$DIGEST
```
That bypasses manifest-list ordering issues.

lisa: we'll also need to regenerate SBOM after any base updates. SBOM job currently runs in the same pipeline but earlier step used a cached layer which may have missed changes. increase SBOM job cache TTL to 0 for builder images so we always run fresh SBOM when base changes.

morgan: CI cost note — full SBOM + license scan runs on a gpu-runner because the test matrix uses CUDA toolchain layers for the infra image, and that runner is expensive. can we move SBOM generation to a smaller runner or use an emulation step?

ian: yes, we can split SBOM step: run SBOM creation inside a lightweight container that just introspects image layers (syft) rather than executing heavy toolchains. syft doesn't need GPU. update job to `sbom: uses: docker://anchore/syft:latest` and analyze the pushed image. cheaper.

sasha: also propose adding a promotion-hook in the image registry: only promote tag to `stable` after the post-push-sign job succeeds. that prevents transient tags pointing to unsigned digests.

infra-ci-bot: TODO created -> #infra/ci (task) -> "publish: sign final digest + sbom on non-gpu runner" assigned to @ian.

lisa: one more gotcha — terraform modules that depend on the builder image reference a tag: `registry.redwood/tools/infra-builder:stable`. If we switch to digest pinning in the CI, we need to write the resolved digest back into the module (or expose a release artifact mapping tag->digest). otherwise infra could pull a different digest later.

morgan: agreed. pipeline should publish a small JSON release manifest to our release-bucket: `{ "tag": "stable", "digest": "sha256:...", "sbom": "s3://.../sbom.json", "signed": true }` and terraform modules can read that via the release data source during apply.

ian: i'll implement minimal change: post-push resolve+cosign sign + upload release manifest + run syft on non-gpu runner. expect a PR today.

sasha: also add a flaky test to detect manifest-list reordering: fetch `crane manifest` and ensure signed digest matches resolved digest. run this in a canary job.

morgan: sweet. for short-term unblock can we manually re-sign the last good digest and re-promote?

lisa: yes i can do manual re-sign and push to `stable` but prefer we land the automation before the next builder release.

morgan: perfect. @ian add the checklist to the PR: pin base in Dockerfile OR document plan to keep tag pinning, add post-push sign, move sbom to syft image, write release manifest, update terraform module to read manifest. thanks all :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: run cleanup job queued: rebuild#4124 scheduled after PR merge.
